title: US SNAP Participation, Mar 2026
question: USDA Food and Nutrition Service SNAP national Average Participation for March 2026, not seasonally adjusted, first-print fixed vintage
resolutionSource: USDA Food and Nutrition Service SNAP Data Tables
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first USDA FNS SNAP monthly national Average Participation value published for March 2026 in the FY2026 national monthly SNAP data table. Convert persons to millions and round to three decimals. Use the first official print only; ignore later revisions or refreshed vintages.

drivers: SNAP caseloads have been nearly flat around 41.7 million in recent official monthly prints
Judgmental macro and household-budget adjustment adds a small upward tilt into early 2026
Judgmental work-requirement, churn, and recertification adjustment offsets part of that upside
March has limited seasonal signal relative to administrative and policy effects
First-print uncertainty is dominated by state reporting lags, policy implementation, and later revision risk

reasoning.text: Forecast for USDA FNS SNAP March 2026 First-Print Participation

The resolver is the first USDA Food and Nutrition Service publication of national SNAP Average Participation for March 2026. The target is an administrative count, not seasonally adjusted, resolved from the official FNS SNAP data table rather than FRED or news mirrors.

reasoning.call: Checked the USDA FNS SNAP data table page for the national monthly SNAP participation series and latest visible reference class.
reasoning.result: Fetched official monthly national Average Participation reference points, converted from persons to millions: FY2025 Mar 41.759 million, FY2025 Jun 41.812 million, FY2025 Sep 41.734 million, and FY2025 Nov 41.687 million; the page also showed Latest Available Month November 2025.

reasoning.call: Checked the official FNS data release calendar / posting schedule for the March 2026 fixed-vintage availability date.
reasoning.result: Fetched the USDA FNS data release calendar entry for SNAP Program Data / monthly SNAP data table refresh showing the March 2026 first-print fixed vintage scheduled for 2026-07-10.

reasoning.call: Checked USDA FNS SNAP program context for scale and administrative mechanism.
reasoning.result: Fetched program context showing SNAP serves about 42 million people nationally and is administered through 50 states plus the District of Columbia, which explains state-reporting lag risk.

reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference-class anchor: recent official monthly participation is tightly clustered around 41.7 million. A neutral outside-view forecast therefore starts near 41.75 million before adding early-2026 macro and policy adjustments.

Model choice: I did not use a formal time-series model because the latest official points show very low short-run trend signal and the largest uncertainty is administrative/policy implementation; a persistence baseline with explicit judgmental adjustments is adequate for this fast public-release forecast.

Level and momentum: the cited latest visible official points range from 41.687 million to 41.812 million, only a 0.125 million span across the selected recent months, so I keep the level close to the 41.75 million baseline and do not extrapolate a large trend.

Current-release adjustments: the +0.20 million macro/need pressure and -0.03 million policy/churn offset are judgmental adjustments, not directly estimated from the FNS historical table. They reflect a small upward demand-risk tilt partly offset by recertification, eligibility, and work-rule churn.

Point calculation: 41.75 million recent baseline + 0.20 million judgmental macro/need pressure - 0.03 million judgmental policy/churn adjustment = 41.92 million. Interval calculation: recent cited official points span only 0.125 million, but the target is several months beyond the latest available print and has policy/state-reporting risk, so I use a judgmental 80% interval about -0.97 to +0.93 million around the point, giving 40.95 to 42.85 million.

Counter-consideration: a downside outside-the-interval case would be rapid enforcement of eligibility or work-rule changes or unusually high procedural churn pushing participation below 40.95 million; an upside outside-the-interval case would be a sharper labor-market deterioration, food-budget stress, or delayed disenrollment pushing participation above 42.85 million.

Review disposition: accepted the reviewer requests to identify the release-calendar entry more specifically, state the persistence-model choice, label the macro and policy adjustments as judgmental, tie the interval to recent observed dispersion plus named policy/reporting uncertainty, keep the policy adjustment consistent at -0.03 million, and clarify that displayed historical values are latest visible official values converted to millions.
